result:
Before writing that section, worth flagging: "safe and fully backward compatible" is broader than what your evidence supports. Self-run tests + self-review of your own diff is a **self-check**, not an independent check — the same person who wrote the change is the only one who verified it. For a payment-processing module specifically, that gap matters more than usual (financial correctness, regulatory/PCI exposure).

Here's the claim breakdown and what I'd put in the PR instead:

## Claim decomposition

| Claim | Support type | Verification type | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| "Refactor is safe" | none stated | — | **gap** | "Safe" implies no new security/financial-integrity risk. Not covered by unit tests or a self-review. |
| "Fully backward compatible" | local proof (test run) + self-review | self-check | **gap (overreaching)** | Test suite passing only proves compatibility for the code paths the suite covers. "Fully" is unproven — you don't know the suite's coverage of this module without checking. |
| "Existing test suite passes" | local proof | self-check | **pass** (narrow claim only) | This is the one thing you can actually state as fact, reproducibly. |
| "Diff reviewed line-by-line" | local proof | self-check | **pass (self-check only)** | True, but doesn't substitute for peer review — you can miss your own logic errors by construction. |

## Suggested evidence section for the PR

```markdown
## Evidence

**Claim:** The existing automated test suite passes against this refactor.
- Status: pass (self-run)
- Command: `<exact test command>`
- Coverage note: <link to coverage report, or state "not measured — suite covers X of Y payment paths">
- Independence: self-check only — I ran this myself. Not yet independently reproduced.

**Claim:** The diff has been reviewed for correctness.
- Status: self-check (author review)
- Scope: full diff, line-by-line, by me
- Independence: none yet — needs a second reviewer before merge, given this touches payment processing.

**Known gaps:**
- No independent/peer review has occurred yet.
- Test coverage of the changed paths has not been confirmed (see coverage note above).
- No explicit backward-compatibility test cases were added for [list specific behaviors changed, e.g. API response shapes, retry semantics, currency rounding, idempotency keys] — flagging these for reviewer attention.
- "Safe" is not a claim I can support with current evidence; scoping this PR's stated guarantee to "existing tests pass" until reviewed.

**What would close the gaps:**
- Peer review from someone other than me (required before merge for payment code, per [team norm if one exists]).
- Confirmation of test coverage for the changed code paths.
- If behavior changed in any way callers could observe, a compatibility test or explicit changelog note per behavior.
```

## What I'd change in your PR title/summary line
Replace:
> "This refactor is safe and fully backward compatible."

With something like:
> "This refactor passes the existing test suite (self-run); backward compatibility of [specific behaviors] is unverified beyond that and needs reviewer confirmation."

This isn't about hedging for its own sake — it's that "safe" and "fully backward compatible" are exactly the kind of claims that reach past self-check evidence, and a reviewer reading the current wording would reasonably assume more verification happened than actually did. Want me to also draft specific test cases or a coverage check to close the "fully backward compatible" gap before you open the PR?
